implementation.status: Plus Jakarta Sans is the single DAYMARK family for headings, tile labels, tile primary lines, tables, and forms. The stacks above are CSS fallbacks. They are not extracted from a reference site.
implementation.loading: Self-host the Plus Jakarta Sans variable TTF (weights 200–800, SIL OFL) with its OFL.txt under the app public/fonts tree, declared with @font-face (font-weight 200 800, font-display: swap). Do not load it from a third-party stylesheet.
implementation.wrapping: Use natural wraps; do not force desktop line breaks on mobile. Tile labels stay short (“Today”, “Confirmation”, “Follow-ups”) and primary lines are one plain sentence (“3 bookings need a reply”). Let controls grow if long translated labels need it.
implementation.metrics: Tabular numerals come from two app classes: .jk-figure (tile primary lines and counts: display family, clamp(1.5rem, 1.2rem + 0.9vw, 2rem), weight 700, -0.025em, line height 1.15, tabular-nums) and .jk-num (tabular-nums only, for times, table cells, and chart labels) so “9:00” and “10:30” align. Tile titles use a title step (1.1875rem, weight 680). Numeric emphasis stays restrained, not oversized hero digits. Check fallback width and layout shift after the variable font loads.
implementation.responsive: Use rem plus viewport terms with clamp; verify actual browser text zoom and narrow reflow. Tiles stack to one column below 48rem, so a primary line must still read at 320px without truncation.
